description: Link two issues: link_issues('PM-419', 'PM-417', 'is blocked by') records that PM-419 is blocked by PM-417. 'type' is the PHRASE, said as a person says it — 'blocks', 'is blocked by', 'duplicates', 'is duplicated by', 'clones', 'relates to' — so the direction is in the words and the arguments cannot disagree; a bare type name ('Blocks') points outward, as it does in Jira. A phrase this workspace does not have is REFUSED and the ones it does have are named, rather than quietly becoming 'relates to'. The link then shows on both issues (get_issue returns 'links'), and linking the same pair the same way again changes nothing. Requires permission to edit BOTH issues — a link is a change to the issue at each end. 'to' may also be an issue of ANOTHER company's PUBLIC project, as 'company/KEY-12' (e.g. 'math/D5-12') or its address there: it is read as somebody with no account reads it, linked only while public, shown in get_issue's 'publicLinks' with a 'state' that says 'unavailable' once its project closes, and the other company is not told. That needs permission to edit 'from' only.

from.description: The issue the phrase is said about, e.g. 'PM-419'.

to.description: The issue at the other end, e.g. 'PM-417' — or another company's public issue, 'math/D5-12'.

type.description: How 'from' relates to 'to', in words: 'blocks', 'is blocked by', 'duplicates', 'clones', 'relates to'. Whatever this workspace's link types call themselves — a refusal lists them.

name: link_issues
title: Link issues
